description.value:
Tier 1 — Storm Wardens

“Weather is only random if nobody is in charge.”

Storm Wardens treat wind, flood, ashfall, and static like administrative problems. They know how to ride a storm front, ground a lightning field, and keep a faction moving when the world is trying to turn travel into a funeral.

You’ve learned the first law of bad weather: panic is usually deadlier than the rain.

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Lore and Faith.
  • Strategic: In hazardous weather or corrupted environmental conditions, your Domain reduces travel and exposure penalties.

“Send the Qliph-Scarred into the bad places. If they come back smiling, it means the rest of probably can still come back.”

Domain Edge. Your Domain leans toward problem-solving in corrupted zones, containment operations, and subtle social pressure.

Corruption-Tuned. You help keep others steady in the presence of Darkness, even when it whispers to you first.

effects.name: Qliph-Scarred: Strategic Hooks (Bad Eden OP Flags)
effects.description: Data-only for your Bad Eden OP and world engines: Qliph-Scarred factions lean toward Intrigue and Non-Lethal lines, especially in corrupted or unstable zones.

description.value:
“Darkness climbed into your bones and decided to stay.”

Shadow Resilience. Your scars drink in hostile power instead of letting it tear you apart.

  • You have resistance to qliphothic damage.
  • Your presence carries a subtle, unsettling weight; you gain a small bonus to Intimidation checks.
  • The deeper interactions with corruption, Qliphothic zones, and Darkness tracks are handled by Bad Eden engines and GM judgment.

effects.name: Qliph-Scarred: Shadow Resilience
effects.description: You have resistance to necrotic damage and a +1 bonus to Intimidation checks. Any extra “corruption handling” stays narrative/BBTTCC-engine side, not automated rolls.

description.value:
A splinter of magenta coral from the reef below the Proving Ground, cold enough to ache through cloth.

Held to the ear it does not sound like the sea. It sounds like the tide going out.

Occult Association (Bad Eden): Prophet / Oracle.

“The future is not hidden. It is just expensive to hear clearly.”

Prophets do not control the future. They endure proximity to it.

Where Tarot Mages manipulate timing and probability like gamblers with dangerous discipline, Prophets stand closer to the signal itself. They hear pattern before it becomes event, consequence before it becomes story, and warning before anyone else admits there is something to warn about.

To a Prophet, the Great Work is not just about choosing well. It is about seeing the shape of what is coming early enough to alter who is prepared for it.

How Prophets pursue the Great Work:

  • By reading emerging pressure before it resolves into action
  • By recognizing encounter patterns before they fully manifest
  • By turning foresight into factional advantage
  • By making ignorance more expensive than preparation

Resonance: Keter / Signal — possibility, revelation, pattern-emergence, and the unbearable weight of glimpsing too much too early.

Tell-tales: pauses before bad news, unfinished sentences that become correct later, eyes that track causes before effects.

Faction Effect (Passive):

  • +1 to Intrigue, planning, or foresight-adjacent OP rolls (GM adjudicates the exact lane)

Cost Principle: foresight creates burden. Expect omen pressure, emotional Stress, false-positive anxiety, and resentment from people who preferred not to know what was coming.

A key of fused slag, still warm no matter how long it sits in a pocket. It anchored the Proving Ground's lava sigil, and it remembers being load-bearing.

What it opens has not been built yet.

"They looked for you in all the usual places. None of them were the right shape."

The Quiet Inside (1/Soma Break). Reaction — when you are targeted by a divination, mind-reading, or truth-detection effect, force the caster to roll their effect against your Resolve instead of its normal save DC.

Failure: the effect returns nothing — no partial information, no awareness that a target was present.

Success: you take 1 point of Stress from the pressure of the probe.

Bad Eden Heritage (v1.1, RFI-native). Qliph-Scarred heritage: Husk.

“What the void took, it didn’t replace. That’s the feature, not the bug.”

Qliph-Scarred (Husk). Your scar is a hollow. Something was removed from you in a place that should have unmade you, and it never got put back. People who try to read you feel the draft. Manifestations that look inside find less to grab. You walked out emptier, and in this world, emptier can mean harder to kill.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Qliph-Scarred).

  • Size. Medium.

  • Movement. 6 squares walking.

  • Lineage Lean. Qliph-Scarred does not grant fixed attribute bonuses; your background handles increases. Your heritage leans toward Mind in fiction and through Tier powers.

Qliph-Scarred Core: What Walked Out

Shared across all Qliph-Scarred heritages. Granted at character creation via the base ancestry item.

  • Shadow Resilience. You have resistance to qliphothic damage. You reroll the lowest die on Body checks against effects that would drain, wither, or corrupt your body.

  • Qliphothic Saturation. Once per scene, when you fail a Soul check, you may reroll it — but your scene's Darkness-gain count increases by 1. The scar pays for what the scar saves.

  • Hunger Mask. You can suppress a bodily need (hunger, thirst, sleep, breath) for up to 24 hours by deciding to; you do not suffer its penalties during that window. At the end of the 24 hours, all deferred needs strike you at once, each as a separate Stress-class consequence.

  • Shadow-Wake. Creatures with qliphothic attunement (demons, corrupt sephirot, Radiation-warped entities) can sense you at 12 squares and know you have been marked. They may not know how to read the mark.

Husk Traits

  • Hollow Core. You have resistance to psychic damage. Creatures attempting to read your thoughts, detect your lies, or determine your emotional state do so rolling 3d10 and keeping the lowest 2. Divination-register effects that would reveal information about you have a 50% chance to return nothing — just the hollow echo of the question.

  • No Weight Inside. You do not need to eat or drink, though you still may. The void is not demanding, once you learn to carry it.

Strategic Hooks (Foundry / Bad Eden)

  • Domain Edge. Your Domain gains +20 Intrigue marks and +10 Non-Lethal marks at campaign start.

  • Hex Synergy. In Empty / Abandoned / Liminal hexes, your Domain's infiltration and passage operations cost 10 fewer marks.

  • Nothing to Grab. Once per turn, when a rival Domain attempts a divination, intelligence, or surveillance operation targeting your Domain, you may force them to reroll that check. They find less than they expected.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Qliphothic Saturation Recovery: 1/scene  ·  Action: Free  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke. Reroll a failed Soul check. Cost: scene's Darkness-gain count goes up by 1.

description.value:
"Act as one."

Mode: Unity · Drift: Toward

Accord makes a squad move like a single animal with too many legs and no argument about which way to run. Your Surge spends turn coordination into mechanics — partners feeding each other rerolls, focus-fire that compounds, a whole line acting on one breath.

Doctrine (spent via Surge)

  • Shared Breath (1) — name an Accord Partner: you and they each bank a reroll-lowest, and they may take a reaction right now.
  • Synchronized Advance (3) — allies within 6 squares bank a reroll on their next attack. Pile onto one target; the second blow lands in the hole the first made.
  • Group Turn (5) — allies within 6 squares each gain a freed bonus action, resolving together.

Out-of-combat: Accord Engine (bend a Parley toward peace), Unity Cadence (Soft Power for a clean scene), and Resonant Truce (the de-escalation aura) remain the strategic flourishes.

"You're not the hero. You're the reason the heroes don't trip over each other."

The Harmony Marshal runs on Surge like everyone — but yours arrives sideways: when an ally within 6 squares lands a surging roll (an exploding 10), the brilliance resonates into you and you bank a Surge too (+1, max +2/round). The party's best moments are your fuel; you spend them feeding the party back. Your tier powers are Surge spends, and the rerolls auto-fire now — no GM bookkeeping:

The Mandate (spent via Surge)

  • Rallying Words (1) — an ally banks a reroll-lowest on their next roll.
  • Ease Attrition (2) — heal an ally and clear one condition.
  • Rally to Me (2) — an ally banks a reroll and frees a reaction.
  • Unity Flourish (3) — every ally within 6 squares banks a reroll.
  • Conductor's Crescendo (5) — the whole line banks a reroll and each clears a condition.

The strategic layer endures out of combat — Attrition Easer, Loyalty Steward, and Unity Conductor still move Soft Power, attrition, and hex loyalty on the campaign turn. In a fight, though, you are a reroll engine: the dice obey you because you asked nicely, at exactly the right moment.

description.value:
Silver Tongue Protocol. You have rehearsed, iterated, and field-tested the art of getting people to actually talk.

  • Whenever you make a Diplomacy (Presence) or Stealth (Intrigue) check, you can treat a rolled result of 8 or lower on the 2d10 as a 9 instead. You can use this feature a number of times per Soma Break equal to your Presence value (minimum once).
  • In Parley, you can spend one use of this feature to reroll the lowest die on a single Influence roll.

(The Active Effect below also gives you a small numeric edge on Diplomacy (Presence) and Stealth (Intrigue) checks as a quality-of-life bonus.)

Crew Type (Bad Eden): Storm Wardens.

“Weather is only random if nobody is in charge.”

Storm Wardens treat wind, flood, ashfall, and static like administrative problems. They know how to ride a storm front, ground a lightning field, and keep a faction moving when the world is trying to turn travel into a funeral.

  • Tactical Identity: You gain a skill rank in Lore and Faith.
  • Strategic Identity: Your Domain starts with +1 Faith OPs.

Tier 1 — Prophet / Oracle

“You don’t know the future. You just know when something has started.”

At Tier 1, you begin catching the edge of events before they fully arrive. Not enough to command them. Enough to stop being surprised.

Tactical (Character Scale)

  • Gain a skill rank in Insight and Perception
  • 1/Soma Break, ask the GM one focused omen-question about an immediate situation, route, or known danger; the answer should be truthful but limited, symbolic, or pressure-based

Strategic (Faction Scale)

  • Once per turn, before a planning-heavy, reconnaissance, or intrigue-forward action, gain +2 to one relevant OP roll by declaring what sign your Domain is acting on

Cost: early warning is rarely comfortable. Expect unease, distraction, or tension when you sense something going wrong before anyone else can justify reacting to it.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Omen Question
Recovery: 1/Soma Break  ·  Action: Free  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke.
Ask the GM one focused omen-question. Truthful but limited / symbolic / pressure-based.

Tier 1 (Level 1) — The Empress (Caretaker)

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Faith and Diplomacy. You learn the Spare the Dying Tier-0 manifestation.
  • Strategic: Your Domain's passive OP bias now follows the base Archetype file.

Peacekeeper's Poise. Your presence steadies people at the exact moment everything could go sideways.

  • When initiative is rolled, you can choose up to a number of creatures equal to your Presence value (minimum one) within 6 squares of you. Each gains temporary Integrity equal to your Presence value + your tier.
  • You can use this feature a number of times per Soma Break equal to your tier.

Qliphothic Saturation. The hollows in you are already full of poison light.

  • You have resistance to poison damage.
  • You often sense when a place is spiritually “overclocked” or unsafe; your scars hum in high-corruption zones.
  • Any radiation/corruption hooks in Bad Eden are driven by flags on this feature rather than automatic rolls.

description.value:
A cheap, mass-produced stiletto with an apology engraved up the fuller. The engraving is competent. The steel is mediocre. The point is sharp. They were sold in bulk before the Shattering as novelty items at gas stations. After the Shattering, somebody noticed they actually work — and not just in the obvious ways.

Mercy Engraving. When you reduce a creature to 0 Integrity with this knife, it falls unconscious and stable instead of dying. The engraved apology counts. Reality accepts the receipt. (Mal: "Don't think about this too hard. The metaphysics are at minimum dubious. The mechanic is real.")

members.name: Corvan Ustile
members.notes: He and Juniper built the leyglass barricade at Mottram Reach board by board, and he still mutters that she left before the last plank was nailed.

members.name: Reine Tocsil
members.notes: Calling the leyline surges costs her a year of smell and taste every time, and Juniper is the only one who still remembers to describe dinner to her.

members.name: Puck Aldery
members.notes: Owes Juniper a debt he can't name out loud — she ran a storm-front alone so he could carry his brother's body out of the Quiet Chair Society's flooded annex, and he's been paying it back in small favors ever since.
